titulo: Advertising: Forms of Persuasion & Advertising Techniques (Aristotle's modes)
resumen:
Ads appear on TV, radio, magazines, billboards, flyers and the Internet (sección 1.1).
The company targets a customer by age, gender, student, marital status and special interest (sección 1.2).
Types of advertising: brand (slogans & jingles), informative and persuasive (sección 1.3).
Forms of persuasion: rational, emotional and positive appeal (sección 1.3).
Aristotle's three modes of persuasion in Rhetoric — logos, ethos and pathos — are used in advertising (sección 1.2 Aristotle).

esquemas.titulo: Using the three modes in an ad
pasos: Logos: the selling proposition, a clear statement + call to action
Ethos: build credibility (testimonials, experts, celebrities, company history)
Combine modes so they complement each other; image, design, casting and sound also persuade

tarjetas.pregunta: What is logos in an ad?
tarjetas.respuesta: The selling proposition or main idea (Aristotle section).

tarjetas.pregunta: Does pathos have to be serious?
tarjetas.respuesta: No; humor also influences emotions (Aristotle section).

tarjetas.pregunta: How many modes does every ad use?
tarjetas.respuesta: At least one; most use two, some all three (Aristotle section).
